# SAT Test Dates 2026: Deadlines, Registration & Scores


## TLDR


The 2026 SAT test dates are March 14, May 2, June 6, August 22, September 12, October 3, November 7, and December 5. As of August 23, 2026, the next SAT is September 12, with a regular registration deadline of August 28 (11:59 p.m. ET). All four remaining fall dates have confirmed score release dates, and registration is open now on College Board’s site.


---


The August 22 SAT is done. If you searched for SAT test dates in 2026 hoping to register for August, you missed it by a day. The good news: four fall dates remain, seats are still available at many test centers, and the September 12 registration deadline is less than a week away.


This guide covers every 2026 SAT date, the deadlines that actually matter (some are earlier than you think), score release timing, fees, and a date-selection framework based on whether you are applying early action, regular decision, or still a junior figuring out your timeline.


Before picking a date, consider taking a[free SAT practice test](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/practice-tests) to see where you stand. A diagnostic score makes the “which date?” question much easier to answer.


> **Quick Answer**
>
>
> The next SAT test date is **September 12, 2026** . The regular registration deadline was **August 28** , but late registration remains available through **September 1, 2026** , subject to availability and additional fees. The remaining 2026 SAT dates are October 3, November 7, and December 5, with scores scheduled for October 16, November 20, and December 18, respectively.
>
>
> If you are trying to register for September 12 after the regular deadline, check College Board immediately because late registration and test-center availability are time-sensitive. All SAT registration deadlines expire at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time.

## SAT Test Dates Glossary


If this is your first time registering, the terminology can be confusing. Here is what each term means and why it matters.


**SAT Weekend.** The standard Saturday SAT where you register yourself, pick a date, and choose a test center. This is what most students mean when they say “the SAT.” The student, not a parent or counselor, must complete registration.


**SAT School Day.** An SAT given during school hours through your school or district. You do not register on your own. For 2026-27, the fall in-school testing window runs October 1 through 30, 2026. If your school offers SAT School Day, ask your counselor about it separately.


**Regular registration deadline.** The last day to register without paying extra. Deadlines close at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time, which catches West Coast students off guard. If you are in California, that is 8:59 p.m. your time.


**Late registration deadline.** The final chance to register after the regular deadline, but it costs an extra $38. This is also the deadline for test center changes and regular cancellations.


**Score release date.** When scores become available in your College Board account. Fall 2026 releases come roughly[13 to 15 days after test day](https://satsuite.collegeboard.org/scores/score-release-dates) . Colleges may take additional time to process scores after receiving them.


**Device lending deadline.** If you need to borrow a testing device from College Board, you must register and request the device[at least 30 days before test day](https://satsuite.collegeboard.org/sat/device-lending) . A request does not guarantee you will receive one.


**Accommodations deadline.** Approval for testing accommodations can take[up to seven weeks](https://accommodations.collegeboard.org/request-accommodations/dates-deadlines) . If you need extended time, a separate room, or other accommodations, the real deadline is much earlier than the registration deadline.


**Sunday testing.** Available only for students who cannot test on Saturday for religious reasons. Fall 2026 Sunday dates are August 23, September 20, October 18, November 8, and December 6.


**Waitlist.** New for fall 2026. When nearby test centers are full,[U.S. students can join a Waitlist](https://allaccess.collegeboard.org/expanding-access-sat-fall-2026-registration-now-open) and be automatically placed when a seat opens up. This does not guarantee a seat, but it is better than refreshing the registration page manually.


**Seat Reserve.** Also new for fall 2026. Participating schools can hold seats for their own students so more people can test in a familiar location.

There is no universally “best” SAT date. The best date is the latest administration that still gives you enough preparation time and produces scores before your college application deadlines.


## Which SAT Date Should You Take?


Use your application deadline and preparation level to choose your test date:


**Need a score for Early Action or Early Decision?**
→ Start with September or October.
→ Check each college's testing deadline before registering.


**Applying Regular Decision?**
→ October or November usually gives you more flexibility.
→ December can work for some January application deadlines, but verify each college's policy.


**You're a junior and aren't applying yet?**
→ You have more flexibility. Choose a date that gives you enough preparation time and leaves room for another attempt in 2027.


**You need a large score improvement?**
→ Do not choose a test date simply because it is soon. Give yourself enough time to prepare between attempts.


**Your preferred test center is already full?**
→ Search other nearby centers, check availability again later, or use College Board's Waitlist option where available. College Board introduced Waitlist and Seat Reserve for fall 2026 to expand access to seats.


## What Is the Next SAT Test Date in 2026?


The next SAT is **September 12, 2026** . The regular registration deadline was August 28, while late registration is available through September 1, 2026. The September SAT score release date is September 25.


If you have not registered yet, do not wait for September 1. Test-center availability can change, and the late-registration deadline is the final registration window listed by College Board for this administration.


After September 12, the remaining 2026 SAT dates are:


-


**October 3, 2026:** scores released October 16


-


**November 7, 2026:** scores released November 20


-


**December 5, 2026:** scores released December 18


## Can You Still Register for the September 12, 2026 SAT?


Yes, but the regular registration deadline has already passed. As of August 29, 2026, College Board lists **September 1, 2026** as the deadline for late registration, changes, and regular cancellations. Late registration costs an additional $38 for students who do not have a fee waiver.


Late registration does not guarantee that your preferred test center will still have a seat. If you need to take the September SAT, check College Board's registration system as soon as possible.


If September is no longer practical, the next SAT dates are October 3, November 7, and December 5.


## Which 2026 SAT Date Should You Choose?


The right date depends on your application timeline, how much prep you have done, and whether you might need a retake. Here is a breakdown by situation.


### Seniors Applying Early Action or Early Decision


Your safest remaining options are September 12 and October 3. September scores release September 25, well before most November 1 and November 15 early deadlines. October scores release October 16, which still gives you a buffer, though it is tighter.


November 7 is risky for early applicants. Scores do not release until November 20, after the most common early deadlines have passed. Some colleges accept self-reported scores and will process official reports that arrive shortly after the deadline, but many do not. Check each school’s policy before banking on November.


A college admissions practitioner on LinkedIn framed it this way: senior year early fall is the time for a final August, September, or October test before early deadlines close. That window is narrow, and it is already half gone.


### Seniors Applying Regular Decision


October 3 or November 7 give you plenty of time. December 5 can work if your colleges clearly accept December scores for January deadlines, but do not make December your first and only attempt. Scores release December 18, and colleges need time to process them. Not sure what score to aim for? Our guide on[SAT scores for colleges](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/sat-scores-for-colleges-ranges-and-admissions-guide) breaks down ranges by school.


### Juniors


You have the most flexibility. Most students take the SAT first in the spring of junior year and again in the fall of senior year. If you are just starting to think about it now, here is a practical plan:


1.


Take a diagnostic to find your baseline.


2.


If you are close to your goal score, consider November or December 2026.


3.


If you need more time to build skills, prepare through winter and take March 2027.


4.


Leave room for May or June 2027 retakes and fall senior-year attempts.


A retired counselor in a Reddit thread on r/ApplyingToCollege suggested November or March for juniors and warned against December if it conflicts with final exams. That is solid advice. Rushing into a test before you are ready wastes money and can be discouraging. If you want to build a structured timeline, this[SAT study schedule guide](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/sat-study-schedule-guide) can help you work backward from your chosen test date.


### Students Whose Local Test Center Is Full


Seat scarcity is real, not hypothetical. Practitioners on Reddit reported that Bay Area students found[zero August SAT seats available](https://www.reddit.com/r/Sat/comments/1u9vjdh/no_seat_is_available_for_the_august_sat_in_the/) weeks before the deadline, forcing them to look at centers hours away or wait for added seats.


College Board responded to this problem by introducing the Waitlist and Seat Reserve for fall 2026 and adding capacity in high-demand areas. If you do not see a convenient center, check back regularly. College Board says availability updates frequently. You can also join the Waitlist to be placed automatically when a seat opens.


The bottom line: the registration deadline and seat availability are two different things. Register early if location matters to you.

## How to Register for the SAT in 2026


SAT Weekend registration is completed through College Board. During registration, students select an available test date and testing location and provide the information required to complete their registration.


The basic process is:


1.


Create or sign in to your College Board account.


2.


Choose the SAT test date you want.


3.


Search for available test centers.


4.


Select your testing location.


5.


Indicate which device you plan to use.


6.


Request a College Board loaned device if you need one and meet the requirements.


7.


Complete payment or apply an eligible fee waiver.


8.


Review your registration details and test-center information.


9.


Before test day, use Bluebook to complete exam setup and obtain your admission ticket.


Register as early as possible if you need a specific location. College Board says fall 2026 includes new Waitlist and Seat Reserve features intended to improve access to test-center seats.

International students pay $68 plus a $43 international fee. Some test centers in select locations add a $24 center fee on top of that.


The first four score reports are free if you order them by nine days after your test date. After that, each additional report costs $15.


**Fee waivers** are available for eligible students, but you should request one at least one to two weeks before the registration deadline. Do not wait until the final day.


**A word about deadline-day surprises.** On August 7, 2026, multiple students on Reddit reported being[charged a late registration fee](https://www.reddit.com/r/Sat/comments/1vhw4z3/late_registration_fee/) for the August SAT even though the regular deadline was that same day at 11:59 p.m. ET. Users said College Board support treated it as an error and issued refunds. Whether this was a system glitch or a timing issue, the lesson is simple: register before the last day whenever possible.

## The Week Before Your SAT: A Checklist


Picking a date is only half the battle. Here is what to do in the days leading up to your SAT.


**5 days before test day:**


-


Download or update the Bluebook app on your testing device.


-


Complete exam setup in Bluebook (this generates your admission ticket).


-


Confirm your test center address and check-in time.


**The night before:**


-


Verify your test center is still open. College Board’s closings page updates every three hours, and[last-minute cancellations do happen](https://satsuite.collegeboard.org/sat/what-to-bring-do/what-to-expect) . Students on Reddit have reported checking Bluebook the morning of the test only to find their center was canceled.


-


Make sure your physical photo ID matches the name on your admission ticket exactly. Digital IDs are not accepted.


-


Charge your device fully and bring your power cord.


**Test day morning:**


-


Arrive by 7:45 a.m. Doors close at 8:00 a.m.


-


If you are using a borrowed College Board device, arrive by 7:15 a.m.


-


Testing starts around 8:15 to 8:30 a.m. and ends around 10:45 to 11:00 a.m. for standard time.


One thing worth emphasizing: the SAT is fully digital. You take it in Bluebook, answers submit automatically, and you have access to digital tools like annotation, cross-out, and a built-in calculator. Several popular test prep sites still mention bringing No. 2 pencils and filling in bubbles. That advice is outdated. If you want to[practice the digital format](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/digital-sat-prep) before test day, do it on the same type of device you will use at the test center.


## SAT Structure: What You Are Actually Sitting For


The digital SAT has two sections, each with two adaptive modules:


-


**Reading and Writing:** 64 minutes total (two 32-minute modules), 54 questions


-


**Math:** 70 minutes total (two 35-minute modules), 44 questions


Total testing time is 2 hours and 14 minutes with 98 questions. The second module in each section adjusts difficulty based on how you performed in the first module. This adaptive design is why[understanding how the digital SAT is scored](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/how-is-the-digital-sat-scored-adaptive-scoring) matters for your prep strategy.


## SAT School Day vs. SAT Weekend


These are two different testing paths, and confusing them is common.


**SAT Weekend** is what this article is primarily about. You register yourself, choose your date and test center, and show up on a Saturday morning. All the dates in the table above are SAT Weekend dates.


**SAT School Day** is administered through your school or district during a weekday testing window. You do not register on your own. For 2026-27, the fall in-school window is October 1 through 30, and the spring SAT School Day window is March 1 through April 30, 2027.


If your school offers SAT School Day, it can be a convenient option, especially if weekend test centers near you are full. Ask your counselor whether your school participates and whether the scores are sent to colleges the same way.


## Planning Beyond the Date: Prep, Retakes, and Score Goals


Choosing a date is a commitment. Once you register, the clock starts on your prep window. A few practical considerations:


**How much study time do you need?** That depends on the gap between your current score and your target. If you are not sure how long to prepare, our breakdown of[how long to study for the SAT](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/how-long-to-study-for-sat-hours-timelines) gives hour estimates based on score-improvement goals.


**Back-to-back SATs are not always productive.** Taking the SAT in September and again in October gives you only three weeks between tests. That is rarely enough time to make meaningful skill improvements. If you need a big score jump, spacing your attempts further apart (September then November, or October then December) gives you real prep time between sittings.


**Register for a retake proactively.** As the retake matrix above shows, you often cannot wait for one score before the next registration deadline passes. Register for a backup date now and cancel if you hit your target. The $34 cancellation fee is worth the peace of mind.


If you are starting prep now for a fall 2026 SAT date, a[guided SAT study plan](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat) can help you focus on the highest-impact skills in whatever time you have left.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the next SAT test date in 2026?


As of August 23, 2026, the next SAT is September 12, 2026. The August 22 SAT has already passed.


### When is the registration deadline for the September 12 SAT?


The regular deadline is August 28, 2026, and the late registration deadline is September 1, 2026. Both expire at 11:59 p.m. ET.


### When do September 2026 SAT scores come out?


College Board lists the September 12 score release date as[September 25, 2026](https://satsuite.collegeboard.org/scores/score-release-dates) .


### Are U.S. and international SAT dates the same?


Yes. College Board’s current dates page states that the listed SAT Weekend dates and deadlines apply to both U.S. and international students. International students pay an additional $43 fee.


### Is the SAT still on paper in 2026?


No. The SAT is fully digital, taken in the Bluebook app. Your answers submit automatically. Some test prep websites still reference paper testing, but that information is outdated.


### What if my test center is full?


U.S. students can join the Waitlist when nearby centers are full. College Board may also add seats at high-demand locations as test day approaches. Search multiple centers and check back frequently.


### How much does the SAT cost?


$68 for U.S. students. Late registration adds $38. International students pay $68 plus a $43 international fee.


### Can I take the SAT on a Sunday?


Only if you cannot test on Saturday for religious reasons. Fall 2026 Sunday dates are available, and you can request Sunday testing during registration.
